title: Is The Occurrence of IgA-Nephropathy modulated by Gene Mutations of Phase 1 and 2 Detoxification Enzymes?
summary: Kidney diseases are in most parts of its origins not well understood. Thus basic strategies for its treatment are lacking. The prevalent chronic kidney disease is IgA nephropathy leading to about 20-30% to kidney dialysis. Our study will find out if patients suffered from IgA nephropathy could be carrier of genetic variants within phase I and/or II enzymes. These enzymes take part in metabolism and detoxification respectively and modulate individual toxicity of xenobiotics. We would like to find out if individually decreased activity of detoxification enzymes are associated with the occurrence of IgA nephropathy in comparison with a control group and with the known spreading of the enzyme variants in the general population.
conditions: CKD with particular reference to IgA nephropathy

interventions.name: A blood sample of patients with IgA nephropathy will be proceeded once to examine the phase I and II gene
Control group with frequencies of enzyme variations in the general population as described in the relevant scientific literature (databases).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Histologic proven IgA nephropathy in Caucasians of either sex 
For the controls: chronic kidney disease patients without glomerulonephritis in Caucasians of either sex 
Further controls: published SNP- frequencies of phase I and II gene (rate of polymorphisms in the general population)
Exclusion criteria:
none
